original_question: If an abelian prodiscrete group is compactly generated and has no nondegenerate compact subgroups, must it be discrete?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Question 7: whether an Abelian prodiscrete compactly-generated group without nondegenerate compact subgroups must be discrete.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the class of groups (abelian prodiscrete groups), the finiteness hypothesis (compactly generated), the exclusion of compact subgroups, and the intended conclusion (discreteness). In substance, it is essentially Question 7 in Section 9.
missing_details: State explicitly that G is a topological group; otherwise terms such as prodiscrete, compactly generated, compact subgroup, and discrete are not fully stand-alone.
Define 'prodiscrete' as a projective limit of discrete groups, equivalently a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups.
Define 'compactly generated' in the topological-group sense: algebraically generated by a compact subset.

Replace or gloss the paper’s phrase 'without nondegenerate compact subgroups' by an explicit stand-alone condition such as 'having no nontrivial compact subgroups' (or no compact subgroup other than the identity subgroup), since that phrase is not defined in situ in the survey.
refined_question: Let G be an abelian topological group that is prodiscrete, i.e. a projective limit of discrete groups (equivalently, a closed subgroup of a product of discrete groups). Suppose G is compactly generated, meaning that G is algebraically generated by a compact subset, and suppose G has no nontrivial compact subgroups. Must G be discrete?
justification: The supplied draft clearly targets Section 9, Question 7 of the paper, and it is already almost verbatim. To make it fully stand-alone, the only real additions needed are the paper’s earlier meaning of 'prodiscrete' from Section 3 and an explicit topological definition of 'compactly generated'. Section 4 gives the relevant structural backdrop for why prodiscrete quotients are central in the abelian theory: every abelian pro-Lie group splits as V x H with H/H0 ≅ G/G0 prodiscrete and every compact subgroup contained in H. Section 9 then isolates exactly your special case as an open problem and points the reader to the compact-generation discussion in [5].
